what we believe

92% of people say they'll "start living" after the next thing.

after the deadline. after the move. after they lose the weight. after they save enough. but the next thing just becomes another reason to wait. we're done waiting. and we think you are too.

"because inspiration fades. living doesn't."

founder of feelslikeee

meet the founder

hey, i'm Sneha.i built this
because i needed it.

i was the kind of person who had 47 browser tabs of things to do someday. cool restaurants, hikes, places to visit, things to try. never went to any of them. kept saying next weekend, next month, when things calm down.

things didn't calm down. but i started going anyway. and it changed everything. feelslikeee club is what i wish had existed when i was still waiting for my life to start.

"you don't need a different life. just a different way of living the one you already have."

how it works

simple enough to actually do.

1

you join feelslikeee club.

one click. that's genuinely the hardest part. everything else just shows up.

2

every Sunday, a challenge lands in your inbox.

named. real. with a story behind it. something you can actually do this week, whether you have 10 minutes or a whole afternoon.

3

you do it. your way.

no right answer. no performance. no one's grading you. just you, doing the thing, making the memory.

4

you share it. the community shows up.

see how others completed the same challenge. different cities, different lives, same Sunday. that's the bit that makes this feel like something real.

5

by December, you have 52 stories.

not 52 plans. not 52 saved posts. 52 things you actually did. a year that felt genuinely different.

ask us anything

got questions? we've got you.

every challenge has versions that take 10 minutes or a whole afternoon. ate lunch outside instead of at your desk? that counts. the challenge fits into your week, not the other way around.
nothing happens. no streaks to lose, no guilt, no catch-up homework. just come back the next Sunday and keep going. life is flexible here.
every Sunday email asks you to go do something. not read something. not save something for later. actually do something. that's the difference.
completely. every challenge can be done alone. the community is there if you want it, never pressuring you if you don't. some of the best stories come from people who did the challenge completely solo.
you could. but you have that list already, don't you? the one you never open. structure and a community doing it with you are what turn good intentions into actual weeks you remember.
yes. no questions, no guilt, no 47 confirmation emails. just cancel and go. though honestly most people don't want to.
